issues.detail: The Hebrew name הֲדַדְעֶזֶר (Hadadezer) is rendered as 大德謝爾, which is a non-standard transliteration; more importantly, the father's name רְחֹב (Rehob) is rendered as 街道 (street), which is a mistranslation of the proper name as a common noun. The phrase '瑣巴王街道的兒子' incorrectly makes '街道' (street) the son of the king of Zobah, whereas the Hebrew says Hadadezer son of Rehob, king of Zobah.

The Hebrew phrase בְּלֶכְתּוֹ לְהָשִׁיב יָדוֹ בִּנְהַר means 'when he went to restore his hand/control at the River (Euphrates)'. The Chinese '當時他正前去大河重掌權柄' conveys this adequately, but the name issue above changes the identity of the person being struck.
